questions.question: Which Indian festival is a festival of lights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diwali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Known as the **Festival of Lights, Diwali** is one of the most popular and widely celebrated festivals in India.
 
• People celebrate by lighting **oil lamps (diyas)**, bursting firecrackers and worshiping deities like **Lakshmi** (goddess of wealth) and Lord **Ganesha**.
 
• Diwali marks the return of **Lord Rama to Ayodhya** after a 14-year exile and his victory over Ravana, according to the Ramayana.
 
• It is typically a five-day festival, with the main celebration on the third day, known as **Lakshmi Puja.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Holi** is celebrated primarily in northern India to welcome the **arrival of spring.**
 
• Holi signifies the **victory of good over evil**, particularly the burning of the demoness **Holika**.
 
• Holi falls on the **Purnima (full moon) day of the Hindu calendar month of Phalguna**, which usually occurs in March.
 
• There are **three types of Bihu celebrated in Assam**:
 
 
• **Rongali Bihu (Bohag Bihu)**: Celebrates the Assamese New Year and is a spring festival.
 
• **Kongali Bihu (Kati Bihu)**: A quieter festival, focused on prayer and lighting of lamps during the month of Kati.
 
• **Bhogali Bihu (Magh Bihu):** Celebrated in January to mark the end of the harvesting season.
 
 
 
• **Onam** is the **biggest festival in Kerala** and celebrates the legendary return of **King Mahabali.**
 
• One of the major attractions during Onam is the famous **snake boat races**, particularly in the** Pampa River**.
 
• Onam falls in the **Malayalam month of Chingam**, which usually occurs in August-September.

questions.question: Which Mughal ruler was responsible for the execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur in the year 1675?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurangzeb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the year 1675, Guru Tegh Bahadur was Killed in Delhi under the orders of the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb, the sixth Mughal emperor, of India.
 
• He was named head of the Sikh community after the death of the seven-year-old Guru Har Krishan.
 
• The name Guru Tegh Bahadur was given to him by Guru Hargobind.
 
• Sikh tradition says that the guru stood up for the interests of Kashmiri Pandits who approached him to intercede with the emperor on their behalf and to urge him to abolish a jizya (tax) recently levied.
 
• Convinced to stand up for the safety of the Kashmiri Pandits by his uncle, Gobind Rai, who later became Guru Gobind Singh, Guru Tegh Bahadur travelled to Delhi.
 
• In the late 17th century, Emperor Aurangzeb of Mughal levied Sharia law throughout his realm and an extra jizya levy on non-Muslims.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• At Bakala, Guru Tegh Bahadur meditated at the place for about 26 years 9 months 13 days.
 
• The ninth of the 10 Gurus of the Sikh religion was Guru Tegh Bahadur, revered as the ninth Nanak.
 
• The ninth of the 10 Gurus of the Sikh religion, Guru Tegh Bahadur died on November 24, in the year 1675.
 
• He is famously known for the protection he provided to the Sikhs and the Hindus against a 17th-century law that forced them to convert to Islam.
 
• His son Guru Gobind Singh, the last Guru of the Sikhs, transformed the community into a martial race to counter the might of the Mughals.
 
• ​Guru Tegh Bahadur was the ninth Sikh Guru, often venerated as the ‘Protector of Humanity’ (Srisht-di-Chadar) by the Sikhs.
 
 
• Known as a great teacher, Guru Tegh Bahadur was also an excellent warrior, thinker, and poet, who wrote detailed descriptions of the nature of God, mind, body, and physical attachments among other things spiritual.
 
• His writings are housed in the sacred text, ‘Guru Granth Sahib,’ in the form of 116 poetic hymns.
 
• He was also an avid traveller and played a key role in setting up preaching centres throughout the Indian subcontinent.
 
• During one such mission, he founded the town of Chak-Nanki in Punjab, which later became a part of Punjab’s Anandpur Sahib.
 
• In the year 1675, Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed in Delhi under the orders of the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb.

questions.question: In which Gharana do singers perform the Khandhar Vani and Gauhar Vani?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Darbhanga Gharana.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Darbhanga Gharana

 
 
• Darbhanga Gharana is known for its distinctive style of singing Dhrupad, which is one of the oldest forms of North Indian classical music.
 
• The Gharana has a rich history and has contributed significantly to the preservation and propagation of Dhrupad music.
 
• Notable features of Darbhanga Gharana include its emphasis on clarity of notes, intricate rhythmic patterns, and powerful vocal delivery.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Some other important Gharana:-**

 
• Jaipur Gharana :

 
 
• The Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana emerged from Alladiya Khan's family which originated from Atrauli and migrated to Jaipur.
 
• The Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana is Hindustani music founded by Alladiya Khan (1855–1946) in the late-19th century.
 
• The Gharana is known for its distinctive vocal aesthetics, raga repertoire, and technical aptitude.
 
• The chief exponents of the Jaipur Gharana are Alladiya Khan, Mallikarjun Mansur, Kesarbhai Kerkar, Kishori Amonkar, Shruti Sadolikar, Padma Talwalkar and Ashwini Bhide Deshpande.
 
 
 
• Patiala Gharana :
 
 
• ‘Patiala Gharana’ is one of the Gharanas in Indian Classical Music, which was founded by Ustad Fateh Ali Khan, and also Ustad Ali Baksh.
 
• Patiala Gharana has both kinds of singing – ‘Thumri’ and ‘Khyal’.
 
• The most famous exponents of Patiala Gharana are Pakistani ghazal singer Gulam Ali, and also the contemporary singer Shafqat Amanat Ali.
 
• Both the Pakistani singers have also garnered enormous fame in India.
 
 
 
• Banaras Gharana :
 
 
• The Benaras Gharana evolved as a result of the great lilting style of khayal singing known by Thumri singers of Benaras and Gaya. 
 
• It was founded by Pt Gopal Mishra.
 
• The chief exponents of the Benaras Gharana are Rajan Mishra, Sajan Mishra, Girija Devi and others. 
 
 
 
• Maihar Gharana :
 
 
• The Maihar Gharana is a Gharana or school of Hindustani classical music, a style of Indian classical music originating in the northern parts of the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about planet Saturn is true?

options.text: Saturn's environment is conducive to life.
Saturn is the fourth planet from the Sun and the largest planet in our solar system.
Saturn is a massive ball made up mostly of nitrogen.
Satellites like Enceladus and Titan of Saturn are home to internal oceans, could possibly support life.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satellites like Enceladus and Titan of Saturn are home to internal oceans, could possibly support life**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Saturn is called "The Jewel of the Solar System". It is a ringed planet.

__
 
• It is the second-largest planet after Jupiter.
 
• Its beautiful rings are not solid. They are made up of *Ice, dust, and rock.*__
 
• Its rings are huge but thin. They can be seen from the earth with the help of a telescope. 
 
• It is very windy on Saturn. Winds around the equator can be 1800 kilometres per hour. On Earth, the fastest winds only get to about 400 kilometres per hour.
 
• Saturn goes around the Sun very slowly. A year on Saturn is more than 29 Earth years. But, it spins at its axis very fast i.e., 10 hours and 14 minutes a day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Solar system: It is the collection of eight planets and their moons in orbit around the sun, together with smaller bodies in the form of asteroids, meteoroids, and comets. The planets of the solar system are (in order of distance from the sun).
 
• The planets are characterized into two: The terrestrial planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars), and The Jovian planets (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune).
 
• The Terrestrial planets have rocky and solid compositions. They are close to the Sun and have few or no Moons. Also, they have no rings around them.
 
• The Jovian planets are also known as Gas planets. They are larger and composed of gas and liquid. They have multiple Moons. They all have some form of rings around them.
 
• Mercury is the smallest planet and Jupiter is the biggest planet.

questions.question: Which of the following isotopes is used as a fuel in nuclear power plants for generating electricity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uranium - 235**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Uranium-235 (U-235)** is a fissile isotope, meaning it can sustain a chain reaction of nuclear fission.
 
• U-235 is used as fuel in **nuclear power plants** to generate electricity.
 
• It is one of the few materials that can undergo nuclear fission, making it crucial for nuclear reactors and nuclear weapons.
 
• Uranium-235 is naturally occurring, but only about **0.7% of natural uranium** is U-235, the rest being Uranium-238.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nuclear Fission**

 
 
• It is the process of splitting a heavy nucleus into two lighter nuclei, accompanied by the release of a large amount of energy.
 
• In a nuclear reactor, when a U-235 nucleus absorbs a neutron, it becomes unstable and splits, releasing energy, more neutrons, and fission products.
 
• The additional neutrons can further induce fission in other U-235 nuclei, creating a self-sustaining chain reaction.
 
 
 
• **Nuclear Power Plants**
 
 
• These facilities use the heat generated from nuclear fission to produce steam, which drives turbines connected to generators, thus producing electricity.
 
• They are considered a low carbon energy source as they do not produce carbon dioxide during operation, unlike fossil fuel-based power plants.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes**
 
 
• Isotopes are variants of a chemical element that have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons in their nuclei.
 
• This results in different atomic masses for the isotopes of the same element.
 
 
 
• **Uranium Enrichment**
 
 
• The process of increasing the proportion of U-235 in natural uranium to make it suitable for use in nuclear reactors or weapons.
 
• Enrichment is typically required because natural uranium's U-235 content is too low for most nuclear reactors.
 
• Common methods of enrichment include gas centrifuge and gaseous diffusion.

questions.question: Where did India win its last Olympic medal in men’s hockey? (As of March, 2024).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tokyo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India won its last Olympic medal in men’s hockey at the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics**.
 
• The Indian men's hockey team clinched the **bronze medal** after defeating Germany 5-4.
 
• This victory marked the end of a **41-year medal drought** in men's field hockey for India at the Olympics.
 
• The medal win at Tokyo 2020 was India's **12th Olympic medal** in men’s hockey.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Olympic Games**

 
 
• The Olympic Games are a leading international sporting event featuring summer and winter sports competitions in which thousands of athletes from around the world participate in a variety of competitions.
 
• The Games are considered the world's foremost sports competition and are held every four years, with the Summer and Winter Games alternating by occurring every four years but two years apart.
 
 
 
• **Men's Field Hockey**
 
 
• Field hockey is a team sport of the hockey family, which is played on grass, watered turf, artificial turf, or synthetic field, as well as an indoor boarded surface.
 
• India has a rich history in men's field hockey, having won numerous medals in past Olympic Games, including eight gold medals.
 
 
 
• **Tokyo 2020 Olympics**
 
 
• The Tokyo 2020 Olympics were originally scheduled to take place in 2020 but were postponed to 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• This edition of the Olympics saw significant safety protocols and restrictions due to the ongoing pandemic.

questions.question: Delhi ridge is the water divide between which of the following rivers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ganges and Indus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Delhi Ridge is a northern extension of the ancient Aravalli Range.
 
• The ridge acts as a natural barrier and water divide between the Ganges and Indus river systems.
 
• It extends from the southeastern parts of Haryana through Delhi to the Yamuna river.
 
• The ridge plays a crucial role in the local climate, biodiversity, and water management of the Delhi region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Water Divide**

 
 
• A water divide, also known as a watershed or drainage divide, is a geographical boundary that separates neighboring drainage basins.
 
• Water divides determine the direction in which water flows and are crucial for managing water resources and preventing floods.
 
 
 
• **Aravalli Range**
 
 
• The Aravalli Range is one of the oldest mountain ranges in the world, dating back to the Proterozoic era.
 
• It runs approximately 692 km across northwestern India, from Delhi to Gujarat.
 
• The range plays a vital role in influencing the climate and hydrology of the region.
 
 
 
• **Ganges River**
 
 
• The Ganges, also known as Ganga, is a major river in the Indian subcontinent, flowing through India and Bangladesh.
 
• It is considered sacred in Hinduism and is vital for agriculture, industry, and domestic use.
 
 
 
• **Indus River**
 
 
• The Indus River is one of the longest rivers in the world, flowing through China (Tibet), India, and Pakistan.
 
• It is a key water source for agriculture and is historically significant as the cradle of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization.

questions.question: The Lucknow Gharana of Kathak was founded by ___________ , a devotee of the Bhakti movement who lived in southeast Uttar Pradesh.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ishwari Prasad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ishwari Prasad** is credited with founding the Lucknow Gharana of Kathak.
 
• He was a devotee of the Bhakti movement.
 
• Ishwari Prasad hailed from southeast Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The Lucknow Gharana is known for its expressive and nuanced storytelling through dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lucknow Gharana of Kathak**

 
 
• The Lucknow Gharana is one of the three main schools of Kathak dance, the other two being the Jaipur and Banaras Gharanas.
 
• It is known for its graceful movements, intricate footwork, and expressive facial expressions.
 
• This Gharana places a strong emphasis on the storytelling aspect of Kathak, often enacting stories from Hindu mythology.
 
• The dancers of this Gharana often use subtle gestures and movements to convey emotions and narratives.
 
 
 
• **Bhakti Movement**
 
 
• The Bhakti movement was a medieval Hindu movement of theistic devotional trend that emerged in the 8th century in South India and later spread to the north.
 
• It emphasized devotion to a personal god and the idea that salvation could be attained through such devotion.
 
• Bhakti poets composed verses in local languages, making the movement accessible to the common people.
 
• It was a reaction against the rigidities of the caste system and aimed to make religious experience more personal and direct.
 
 
 
• **Kathak Dance**
 
 
• Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.
 
• The word Kathak is derived from the Vedic Sanskrit word Katha, meaning "story," and Kathakar, meaning "the one who tells a story."
 
• The dance form traces its origins to the itinerant bards of ancient northern India, known as Kathakars or storytellers.
 
• Kathak evolved during the Bhakti movement and was later influenced by the Mughal era, incorporating elements of Persian dance and music.

• Founded in 1966 by Bal Thackeray, Shiv Sena is a right-wing Marathi regional and Hindu nationalist political party in India.

questions.question: In which year did Swami Vivekananda give his speech at the Chicago Parliament of Religions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1893**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Swami Vivekananda delivered his famous speech at the Parliament of Religions in Chicago on **11th September 1893**.
 
• His speech began with the words "Sisters and Brothers of America," which received a standing ovation from the audience.
 
• The speech is considered a watershed moment in the history of India's religious and cultural influence on the West.
 
• Swami Vivekananda emphasized the importance of religious tolerance and universal acceptance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parliament of Religions**

 
 
• The Parliament of Religions was an event held in 1893 as part of the World's Columbian Exposition in Chicago.
 
• It aimed to create a global dialogue on religious matters and promote understanding between different faiths.
 
• It was the first formal gathering of representatives from Eastern and Western spiritual traditions.
 
 
 
• **Swami Vivekananda**
 
 
• Born as Narendranath Datta on 12th January 1863, Swami Vivekananda was a key figure in introducing Indian philosophies of Vedanta and Yoga to the Western world.
 
• He was a chief disciple of the 19th-century Indian mystic Ramakrishna.
 
• Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission and the Ramakrishna Math, which continue to promote his teachings and humanitarian activities.
 
• He played a significant role in the revival of Hinduism in India and contributed to the concept of nationalism in colonial India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Speech**
 
 
• The speech marked the beginning of global recognition for Indian spirituality and philosophy.
 
• It helped dispel many prejudices about Indian culture and religion in the West.
 
• Swami Vivekananda's address is often cited as a pivotal moment in the history of interfaith dialogue.

questions.question: Which Commission drew the boundary line between India and Pakistan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radcliffe Boundary Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Radcliffe Boundary Commission was established in 1947 to demarcate the boundary between India and Pakistan.
 
• The commission was chaired by Sir Cyril Radcliffe, a British lawyer.
 
• It was formed as part of the Indian Independence Act 1947, which led to the partition of British India.
 
• The boundary line drawn by the Radcliffe Commission is known as the Radcliffe Line.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hilton Young Commission**

 
 
• Also known as the Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance, it was established in 1926.
 
• It played a significant role in the establishment of the Reserve Bank of India in 1935.
 
 
 
• **Bretton Woods Commission**
 
 
• The Bretton Woods Conference in 1944 led to the establishment of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank.
 
• It played a crucial role in shaping the post-World War II global economic order.
 
 
 
• **Gandhi Irwin Pact**
 
 
• Signed on March 5, 1931, between Mahatma Gandhi and Lord Irwin, the then Viceroy of India.
 
• The pact marked the end of the civil disobedience movement and led to the release of political prisoners.
 
 
 
• **Radcliffe Line**
 
 
• The Radcliffe Line is the boundary demarcation line between India and Pakistan, drawn in 1947 upon the Partition of India.
 
• The line divides the Indian subcontinent into two nations: India and Pakistan.
 
• The demarcation was based on religious majorities, with areas predominantly Muslim becoming part of Pakistan and areas predominantly Hindu remaining in India.
 
• It led to one of the largest mass migrations in human history and significant violence and turmoil.

questions.question: The Fundamental Duties of Citizens were introduced by the 42nd Amendment in the year:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1976**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties of Citizens were introduced by the 42nd Amendment Act in the year **1976**.
 
• This amendment was enacted during the period of Emergency in India (1975-1977).
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Initially, ten Fundamental Duties were incorporated in the Indian Constitution under Article 51A.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976:**

 
 
• Known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its wide-ranging impact on the Indian Constitution.
 
• It was passed during the period of Emergency under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's government.
 
• Besides introducing Fundamental Duties, it also made significant changes to the Preamble, Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles, and the structure of the Parliament and Judiciary.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties:**
 
 
• These duties are intended to remind citizens of their moral obligations towards the nation and fellow citizens.
 
• They are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
• Initially, there were ten Fundamental Duties, but the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added one more duty, making the total count eleven.
 
 
 
• **Swaran Singh Committee:**
 
 
• This committee was constituted in 1976 to make recommendations for the inclusion of Fundamental Duties and other constitutional changes.
 
• It was headed by Swaran Singh, a senior Congress leader and former Union Minister.
 
• The committee's recommendations led to the incorporation of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Emergency (1975-1977):**
 
 
• It was a 21-month period when President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed, upon the advice of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, declared a state of emergency across the country.
 
• During this period, civil liberties were suspended, and many political opponents were imprisoned.
 
• This period saw significant constitutional changes, including the 42nd Amendment Act.

questions.question: The Parliament of India has passed the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act 2002, which establishes the basic rights of primary education for children between:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 - 14 Years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act was passed by the Parliament of India in December 2002, and it came into effect on July 1, 2003.
 
• This amendment inserted Article 21A in the Constitution, making education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• It made it mandatory for the State to provide free and compulsory education to all children in this age group.
 
• The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, was enacted to operationalize this constitutional mandate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Amendment:**

 
 
• A constitutional amendment is a change made to the Constitution of a country, which requires a specific procedure to be followed for its adoption.
 
• In India, a constitutional amendment requires a special majority in both houses of Parliament and, in certain cases, ratification by at least half of the state legislatures.
 
 
 
• **Article 21A:**
 
 
• Article 21A was added to the Indian Constitution by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act.
 
• It stipulates that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years in a manner determined by law.
 
 
 
• **Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009:**
 
 
• The RTE Act was enacted to give effect to Article 21A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It mandates that every child has a right to full-time elementary education of satisfactory and equitable quality in a formal school which satisfies certain essential norms and standards.
 
• It also lays down the responsibilities of the State, parents, schools, and teachers to ensure the implementation of this right.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Amendment:**
 
 
• This amendment has significantly increased the enrollment rates in primary schools across India.
 
• It has also brought attention to issues such as infrastructure, quality of education, and teacher training in the Indian educational system.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement/(s) is /are true with respect to Supreme Court Observation in A.G. Perarivalan vs The State Of Tamil Nadu State?

1. It highlighted that the Governor’s powers are qualified by the constitutional mandate, chiefly requiring them to act in aid and advice of the council of ministers

2. The bench headed by justice L Nageswara Rao ordered the freedom of one of the convicts in the Rajiv Gandhi assassination case.

3. The bench was of the opinion that there are three sources of power-Governor, Council of Ministers and the Constitution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Governor's Powers:** The Supreme Court highlighted that the Governor's powers are qualified by the constitutional mandate, chiefly requiring them to act in aid and advice of the council of ministers.
 
• **Convict's Release:** The bench headed by Justice L Nageswara Rao ordered the freedom of one of the convicts in the Rajiv Gandhi assassination case.
 
• **Bench Composition:** The Supreme Court bench included Justice L Nageswara Rao and other justices who were instrumental in making the decision regarding the convict's release.
 
• **Constitutional Mandate:** The observations made by the Supreme Court emphasized the constitutional mandate that guides the Governor's actions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governor's Role:**

 
 
• The Governor of a state in India acts as the nominal head, while the real powers of governance lie with the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers.
 
• The Governor is appointed by the President of India and holds office at the President's pleasure.
 
• The Governor's actions and decisions are generally based on the advice of the Council of Ministers, except in certain exceptional situations where they may act at their discretion.
 
 
 
• **Rajiv Gandhi Assassination Case:**
 
 
• Rajiv Gandhi, the former Prime Minister of India, was assassinated on May 21, 1991, by a suicide bomber from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).
 
• Several individuals were convicted in connection with the assassination, and the case has seen numerous legal proceedings over the years.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court's Observations:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court's observations in this case underscore the importance of constitutional principles in guiding the actions of state authorities, including the Governor.
 
• The case highlights the delicate balance of power between the different branches of government and the role of the judiciary in upholding constitutional mandates.
